sources: Montaiglon (ed.), Proces-verbaux de l'Academie royale de peinture et de sculpture 1648-1793, tome III (1689-1704), Paris: J. Baur, 1880, p. 268, assembly of 6 July 1699: a 'Discours sur la necessite ... d'establir des principes certains a la Peinture et a la Sculpture'. Scan: archive.org procsverbauxde03acaduoft

Same volume, p. 268 (6 July 1699): the Protector 'a fort recommande a la Compagnie d'en faire le cas qu'il merite' and said the Academie should address him through De Piles. Earlier, p. 259 (25 April 1699): the Compagnie invites him to take a seat among the Conseillers honoraires. The Discours is transcribed from p. 269 (to about p. 273), and on 24 July 1699 the Compagnie re-read it as a body ('du Discours de M' De Piles, cy-devant transcript', p. 274): the formal act that makes this 'field' under the level rule.

De Piles, Cours de peinture par principes, Paris: Jacques Estienne, 1708, 'La Balance des Peintres', pp. 489-490: 'J'ay fait cet essai plutot pour me divertir que pour attirer les autres dans mon sentiment'; made at the request of 'quelques personnes'; 20 degrees. Scan: archive.org bub_gb_NlS7XHJ_tuYC (OCR read; privilege 23 Jan 1708, approbation of the censor Raguet 19 Jan 1708 on the whole book: 'tres-utile et tres-agreable au Public')

J. Richardson, An Essay on the Theory of Painting, London: W. Bowyer for John Churchill, 1715, p. 230-231: the scale 'is Curious, and Useful' but 'gives not a just Idea of the Masters' (Rembrandt rated above Michelangelo). Two Discourses, London: W. Churchill, 1719, discourse I, p. 55 (folio read from OCR): 'with a little Alteration and Improvement may be of great use to Lovers of Art, and Connoisseurs', then pp. 55-56 his own revised scale. A single connoisseur adopting the scale with corrections, 6 years after De Piles's death (Procès-verbaux IV, p. 81 by inference from the next page header, assembly of 6 April 1709: died 'hier, cinquieme du present mois'). Scans: archive.org bim_eighteenth-century_an-essay-on-the-theory-o_richardson-jonathan_1715, twodiscoursesies00rich

Mairan, 'Remarques sur la Balance des Peintres de M. de Piles', Memoires de l'Academie royale des sciences, annee 1755 (Paris: Imprimerie royale, 1761), Memoires p. 1 ff.; summary in the Histoire, section Geometrie, p. 79: 'L'idee de M. de Piles est ingenieuse et nouvelle' but 'il n'en est pas de meme du cote de l'execution'; Mairan's main correction is that the four degrees should be multiplied, not added. Mairan adopts the idea as 'essais de justesse'. Scan: archive.org histoiredelacad55acad. The spec attaches this item to De Piles; the v0.1 transcription had wrongly placed it under Richardson.

Graddy, 'Taste Endures! The Rankings of Roger de Piles (d. 1709) and Three Centuries of Art Prices', Journal of Economic History 73(3), 2013, pp. 766-791, doi 10.1017/S0022050713000600 (abstract read via Crossref: his overall ratings 'have withstood the test of a very long period of time'); Ginsburgh and Weyers, 'De Piles, Drawing and Color. An Essay in Quantitative Art History', Artibus et Historiae 23(45), 2002, pp. 191-203 (citation verified via Crossref; text not read in full). Scholars treating the ratings as a usable instrument is recorded as a field-level grant; predictive power is NOT counted as proof he was right.

Traduit de l'Anglois, revu et corrige par l'Auteur' (nine years after 1719; Richardson d. 1745). A translation exists and the author revised it; no sales or review evidence was found. Scans: archive.org bub_gb_54yu83dWracC, bub_gb_CMR_s1fWdKkC

James Northcote, Memoirs of Sir Joshua Reynolds, London: Henry Colburn, 1813, p. 179: of Richardson's 'Science of a Connoisseur' 'The whole subject is well handled by Richardson, and may be read with pleasure'. One painter-biographer, 68 years after Richardson's death; the praise is for how the Science treats one subject (Ugolino) and is read here as mild approval of the work, not as a verdict on the connoisseurship claim. (Not coded: Northcote pp. 10-11 say Reynolds as a boy read Richardson's Theory of Painting and had his 'first fondness for his art excited' by it; that is reception of the Theory, undated, not of the connoisseurship claim.) Scan: archive.org memoirsofsirjosh01nort
